Command history writes every submitted command to a temporary file. An
abnormal JVM exit can leave that file behind with contact details readable.

Keep command history entirely in memory while preserving Up and Down recall.
Remove file creation, append, cleanup, and related I/O error paths.

Add a forced-exit regression test to verify that no readable history file
remains, and update the developer documentation.

commitResults.messageBody:
The abnormal-exit test accepts exit code 1 without confirming that the
subprocess added a command. Startup failures can therefore produce a false
pass.

Use a distinctive halt code and require a flushed completion marker emitted
after the command is added. This ensures the test exercises the intended
abnormal-exit scenario before checking for history files.

commitResults.messageBody:
## Summary

Update `delete INDEX` to meet the F4 specification:

* Validate argument count and index format with exact error messages, including oversized integers.
* Delete the selected contact from the currently displayed list while preserving the active filter, remaining order, and other contacts’ information.
* Save a prepared deletion before updating the live model; use atomic file replacement to preserve existing data on save failure.
* Display the required success and empty-list messages, maintain consecutive numbering, and clear input only on success.
* Update user/developer documentation and manual testing instructions.

## Follow-up

Persistent contact-details panel behavior remains with the view-feature owner. The current `view` command displays details in the feedback box.

commitResults.messageTitle: Record undo history for contact changes
commitResults.messageBody:
Contact-changing commands save their results without retaining the
previous contact data.

Undo needs snapshots captured through normal command execution

Introduce UndoableCommand and connect supported commands to session
snapshot storage. Remove session backups during shutdown

Register history only after saving succeeds so failures preserve the
live model, displayed contacts, saved data and existing history

Contact changes retain snapshots, but users cannot restore them through
a command.

Expose history through an argument-free undo command.

Implement UndoCommand using the existing staged-command flow and inject
a narrow UndoHistory dependency through the parser.

Keep undo behavior in the command and persistence orchestration generic.
Consume history only after saving succeeds.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update documentation to record undo behaviour
Add independent contact collections to the model
commitResults.messageBody:
The model holds one address book, and staged commands copy only that
collection.

Favourites need independent data so editing or deleting a contact in one
collection does not affect the other.

Add Contacts and Favourites sections, route model operations to the
active collection, and preserve both in staged commands.

Reuse the existing Model API so contact commands can operate on either
collection without duplicating their logic.

The model supports two collections, but users cannot switch between
them. Startup and command saving still use only the main data file.

Users need to select a collection and manage its contacts without
changing the other collection.

Add the tab command, load favourites at startup, and update the
displayed section, contact list, and save location.

Route both save paths through the selected collection to preserve
save-before-apply guarantees while reusing existing commands.

Users can switch collections but must manually re-enter contacts to add
them to Favourites.

Existing contacts need a direct way to become independent favourites
without losing their details.

Add favourite INDEX with displayed-index validation, duplicate
detection, and a separate error when run from Favourites.

Track the changed collection separately from the active section so
favouriting saves only Favourites while preserving the current Contacts
view and its search filter.

commitResults.messageTitle: Include group changes in undo history
commitResults.messageBody:
Undo detects changes only in people, and group commands do not register
snapshots. Group changes can therefore bypass history.

Include groups when comparing snapshots and make group commands undoable
through the existing shared execution path.

This preserves full address-book restoration without adding
command-specific undo logic.

Undo currently supports only Contacts, leaving Favourites changes
without a recovery path.

Maintain independent histories for each section and register snapshots
for the collection a command changes.

Use the changed section when capturing snapshots so favourite records
Favourites data while Contacts remains active.

commitResults.messageTitle: Preserve undo history across normal restarts
commitResults.messageBody:
Shutdown currently deletes undo snapshots, so reopening the app loses
all available history.

Retain snapshots and atomically save their ordering on shutdown. Reload
validated history only when its checksum matches the saved collection.

Keep each collection's history beside its data file and invalidate the
saved index before changes to prevent stale reuse.

commitResults.messageTitle: Recover undo history after interrupted operations
commitResults.messageBody:
History currently persists only on normal shutdown, leaving interrupted
saves and undo operations without reliable recovery.

Journal both possible histories before replacing collection data.
Recover the history matching the saved file's checksum without
overwriting that file.

Give prepared changes a generic save hook so undo journals snapshot
consumption before publishing its restoration.

Switching sections resets the previous search and display order.

This loses the user's place when navigating between Contacts and
Favourites.

Retain each section's filtered and sorted views during the session. Bind
recent ordering to the collection that owns the view.

Reusing observable views preserves filters and ordering while reflecting
changes made when a section is inactive.

The guides describe section switching as resetting searches.

This conflicts with the retained search and ordering behaviour.

Update navigation guidance, implementation details, and manual checks to
describe independent section views.

Clarify the session boundary and how list reveals contacts hidden by a
retained search.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align undo code with project coding standards
commitResults.messageBody:
Several undo helpers use noun names, recovery flags omit boolean
prefixes, and method headers use inconsistent Javadoc formatting.

These differences make the code harder to read consistently with
the project standards.

Rename helpers, collections, and boolean flags, and normalize
Javadoc headers without changing behavior.

Keep the cleanup separate so the functional changes remain easy
to review. Validate with the existing Gradle checks.

Undo history stores collection data without recording which
operation produced each snapshot.

Descriptive feedback needs to stay aligned with history across
restarts, failed saves, and interrupted operations.

Store descriptions in the recovery metadata and keep them aligned
when snapshots are consumed or evicted. Preserve generic feedback
for older indexes without descriptions.

Extend focused storage tests for persistence, recovery, capacity,
and legacy compatibility.

commitResults.messageTitle: Identify the operation reversed by undo
commitResults.messageBody:
Undo reports the same success message for every restored change.

Users cannot confirm which operation or contact was affected when
several recent changes are available.

Have undoable commands describe their changes and display the
stored description after successful restoration. Include the
contact name or the affected section as appropriate.

Capture descriptions before publishing changes so filtering and
renaming cannot change the identified contact. Validate operation
feedback and retain compatibility with older history.

Contacts cards do not indicate existing favourites.

Users discover a match only when favouriting again fails.

Add yellow stars using the existing contact identity rule. Refresh
indicators after successful commands and section changes.

Compute membership from Favourites without storing extra state. Document
the affected APIs using the required Javadoc format.

Contacts have no identifier independent of their details.

Mirrored favourites need stable identity across edits and reloads.

Assign UUIDs to contacts and persist them in JSON. Preserve IDs
through edits, copies, and undo snapshots. Accept missing IDs in
older files and reject invalid or duplicate stored IDs.

Keep value equality and phone/email duplicate detection unchanged
to preserve existing command behaviour during this increment.

Validate ID persistence, edits, undo, and invalid input through
backend tests. Checkstyle and whitespace checks pass.

Storage saves Contacts and Favourites independently.

Mirrored changes need both files to remain consistent when a save
fails or is interrupted.

Add a coordinated saver that prepares both candidates before
publication. Retain original bytes in a rollback journal and
restore pending saves before retrying.

Keep the journal until both replacements succeed so interrupted
operations can recover missing files and exact original contents.
Leave command integration for the shared undo increment.

Verify with 392 backend tests, Checkstyle, and whitespace checks.
No UI tests are added or run.

commitResults.messageTitle: Share undo history across contact sections
commitResults.messageBody:
Contacts and Favourites maintain separate undo histories.

Mirrored operations need one chronological history so undo cannot
reverse unrelated changes in the other section.

Capture both collections per operation and restore them together. Save
the shared history index with both files in the recovery transaction.
Retain five operations across application restarts.

Keep the active section selected and reset restored views to show all
contacts. Remove obsolete per-section recovery code and tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mirror changes to matching favourite contacts
commitResults.messageBody:
Contacts and Favourites keep independently edited copies.

Stale favourite details can block favouriting another contact.

Mirror edits by persistent ID and validate both collections. Remove
matching favourites when Contacts entries are deleted or cleared. Keep
Contacts unchanged when favourites are removed.

Keep mirroring in the model and reuse coordinated saving and shared undo
in Logic. Preserve local group membership updates.

Preserve unrelated files after load failures
commitResults.messageBody:
Startup substitutes an empty collection when a saved file fails to load.
Subsequent saves write both collections, including that fallback.

Changing the healthy section can therefore overwrite the failed file
before the user has an opportunity to repair it.

Track failed loads and preserve unchanged failed sections during saves
and undo. Allow deliberate changes to replace the affected file. Update
recovery metadata, history fingerprints, and the User Guide.

Selecting files within the existing transaction preserves coordinated
saving and shared undo while keeping explicit repair commands usable.

commitResults.messageTitle: Identify group members by contact ID
commitResults.messageBody:
Groups identify members by name, so deleting one of two contacts
with the same name can remove the other's membership. Name-based
commands also cannot select a specific contact.

Store memberships by persistent contact ID and migrate existing
groups when loading saved data. Allow selection by displayed index
and reject ambiguous names so deletion affects only the intended
member.

The group usage message combines operations on pipe-separated lines,
making valid syntax hard to scan after an invalid command.

Show each operation separately with a concrete example and use the
standard invalid-command heading

commitResults.messageTitle: Filter command: clarify empty result message

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the active tag filter beside the list
commitResults.messageBody:
Viewing a filtered contact replaces the result box with that
contact's details.

Later index commands then use a subset the user can no longer see.

Let's show "Active filter: TAG" above the contact list while a tag
filter is active, and hide it when the list is no longer filtered.

The indicator stays in place when view, edit, or delete replaces the
result message.

commitResults.messageTitle: View command: treat huge indexes as out of range
commitResults.messageBody:
view 2147483648 reports "Invalid command format!".

That value is a positive integer. It is only larger than any
displayed contact, so the format message mislabels a valid index.

Let's accept positive integers of any size and report the usual
out-of-range message when the index is not on the displayed list.

Indexes that are not positive integers, such as words or zero, still
use the invalid-format message.
